answer: Verifiable Ocean Lagoon Randomness assigns each agent a unique identity verified by unpredictable ocean-generated terrain data. Attackers cannot precompute identities, as each requires solving a lagoon-based cryptographic puzzle tied to real-time ocean measurements. The per-identity cost scales with the computational effort to reverse-engineer the lagoon's dynamic randomness, making mass identity creation prohibitively expensive. To prevent physical clustering, the system enforces a strict spatial buffer across the terrace.
